findings.title: Breaking API rename without updating the in-repo web client
findings.explanation: The response field `amount` is renamed to `amount_cents`, but `web/src/api/invoices.ts` still types the field as `amount`, and `web/src/components/InvoiceRow.tsx:10` still renders `invoice.amount / 100`. After this change `invoice.amount` is `undefined`, so the UI shows `NaN` (formatted as 'NaN' or '$NaN') for every invoice. Update the web type and component in this PR (`amount_cents`).

findings.title: Hard rename breaks existing external API consumers and rolling deploys
findings.explanation: Removing `amount` outright breaks any API client, integration, or cached frontend bundle that still reads it. During a rolling deploy, old frontend or clients hitting new backends will break. Return both `amount` (marked deprecated) and `amount_cents` for a deprecation window, or version the API. Remove `amount` once consumers have migrated. Document the change in the changelog or API docs.

findings.title: Internal naming is still ambiguous and Number() on BIGINT is imprecise
findings.explanation: The DB column and `InvoiceRow.amount` are still named `amount`, so the ambiguity remains internally (`payments.ts` also passes `amount` to the provider). Consider aliasing in the SQL (`amount AS amount_cents`) and renaming the row field. Also, `Number()` on a BIGINT loses precision above 2^53. This is unlikely for cents, but worth noting.
